\Cref{fig:1-challenges} connects three challenges to the mechanisms and
evidence used to address them.

First, the primary codebook has useful mathematical structure that a direct
GPU port can overlook. Each eight-bit subspace code indexes 256 distances.
Its Cartesian coordinates permit an exact 16+16 factorisation, but more
aggressive splitting adds lookups and arithmetic. The challenge is to exploit
separability without assuming that the smallest table gives the fastest
scan. Candidate-parallel word access and residual lane cooperation also need
different data mappings.

Second, local quotas can lose global winners. For disjoint groups $U_1,U_2$ and $c=4$, consider
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Top}_4(U)&\subseteq U_1,\\
 \left|\operatorname{Top}_4(U)\cap
 \bigl(\operatorname{Top}_2(U_1)\cup\operatorname{Top}_2(U_2)\bigr)\right|
 &=2<4.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Groups need coverage before merging. Bounds reduce maintenance; scheduling controls parallelism. IVF routing is separate.

Third, reference agreement cannot fix reference error. A $k=1$ counterexample is
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha=\mathcal R_{\rm ref}=\{a\},\quad
 \mathcal T_1=\{b\},\quad a\ne b
 \ \Longrightarrow\ 
 D_S(\alpha)=0,\quad \Recall@1=0
 \qquad(S=1).
\]
We test quality alongside calibration/reuse cost.

\subsection{From database IDs to list-ordered positions}

An input row has identifier $i\in\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. Coarse assignment
places its transformed vector in a list according to the computed
centroid scores. The mathematical assignment target is
\begin{equation}
 a(i)=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{0\leq\ell<n_{\rm list}}
       \|\Pi x_i-\mu_\ell\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:4-assignment}
\end{equation}
Its implementation uses the selected numerical assignment path. Encoding
the primary and residual representations does not subtract $\mu_{a(i)}$;
list membership restricts the future search universe independently of
those reconstructions.

The builder sorts assignments together with a sequence of input IDs.
Let $\rho(p)$ be the input ID at sorted physical position $p$ and let
$o_\ell$ be the start of list $\ell$. The completed arrays satisfy
\begin{equation}
 0=o_0\leq o_1\leq\cdots\leq o_{n_{\rm list}}=N,
 \qquad p\in[o_\ell,o_{\ell+1})\Longrightarrow a(\rho(p))=\ell.
 \label{eq:4-offsets}
\end{equation}
Lower-bound searches give offsets, with
\[
 o_\ell=o_{\ell+1}\Longleftrightarrow\text{list }\ell\text{ is empty}.
\]
Positions are stable within a snapshot, not across builds. All arrays use the same $\rho(p)$.

\begin{figure}[!htbp]
\centering
\input{variants/thesis2/figures/physical-layout}
\caption[Physical GPU index layout]{Physical GPU index layout (schematic).
IVF offsets delimit contiguous physical-position ranges. Independent ID,
word-group-major primary, row-major residual and correction arrays share
position $p$. Byte offsets are relative to each allocation; the illustration
implies neither interleaved allocation nor measured memory transactions.}
\label{fig:4-layout}
\end{figure}

IDs map $p\mapsto\rho(p)$. Two-pass add temporarily builds $\rho^{-1}$ for scatter. Primary ties use positions; final ties use database IDs.

\subsection{Exact addresses and representation widths}

For primary byte $Z[m,p]$,
\[
 \operatorname{offset}_{\rm byte}(Z[m,p])=mN+p.
\] Final packing produces
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf w[j,p]=\sum_{t=0}^{3}2^{8t}Z[4j+t,p],\qquad
 \operatorname{addr}_{\rm byte}(\mathsf w[j,p])=4(jN+p).
 \label{eq:4-primary-address}
\end{equation}
Here $j=0,\ldots,M/4-1$. $\text{word-layout build}\Longrightarrow M\bmod4=0$; other $M$ are rejected. A separate byte-layout compilation
retains the byte representation. Each packed array occupies $NM$ bytes,
but repacking temporarily holds both old and new copies, costing $2NM$.
The one-pass builder
temporarily gathers a vector-major $[N,M]$ primary array, transposes it, and
then repacks; each obsolete copy is freed. The two-pass builder scatters
directly into the subspace-major array before the same final repack.
The search-time lane mapping is discussed in \Cref{sec:5-3}.

Residual codes remain row-major, with
$b_r=\lceil dB_r/8\rceil$ bytes per vector. In the eight-bit configuration,
coordinate $t$ of row $p$ is at byte offset $pb_r+t$. In the four-bit
path it is in byte $pb_r+\lfloor t/2\rfloor$, with even coordinates
in the low nibble and odd coordinates in the high nibble. A four-byte
correction per physical row stores
\begin{equation}
 \gamma[ p ]=2\langle\widehat p(x_{\rho(p)}),
                              \widehat r(x_{\rho(p)})\rangle.
 \label{eq:4-correction}
\end{equation}
Its value must move with that row's codes during gathering or scattering.

List-order primary scans fetch residuals only for survivors. Raw FP32 reranking would add $4Nd$ device bytes. Here compressed reconstructions are refined; Chapter 7 measures recall.

Let $K_{(c)}$ be the global $c$th key when $|U|\geq c$. If a group holds
$c$ distinct, fully scored candidates, the largest key among those
witnesses, $\tau_j$, satisfies $K_{(c)}\preceq\tau_j$. There are already
$c$ candidates no later than $\tau_j$ in the global universe. The shared
bound is initialised to a top sentinel and updated by
\begin{equation}
 \tau\leftarrow\min_{\prec}(\tau,\tau_j).
 \label{eq:5-shared-update}
\end{equation}
No bound is published from fewer than $c$ valid candidates. If the entire
universe has fewer than $c$, no group can publish such a bound and all
valid candidates remain eligible.

\begin{resultblock}
\begin{proposition}[Safe rejection by a witnessed bound]
\label{prop:5-shared-bound}
Assume fixed keys, publications backed by $c$ distinct candidates, and
reads that return either the initial sentinel or one complete published
key. Rejecting a candidate only when $K_q(x)\succ\tau$ cannot remove a
global top-$c$ candidate, irrespective of publication timing.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
A publication has a set $W_\tau$ of $c$ distinct witnesses:
\[
 \max_{x\in W_\tau}K_q(x)\preceq\tau
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad K_{(c)}\preceq\tau.
\]
Sentinel reads and minima of published keys obey the same inequality. Thus
\[
 x\in\operatorname{Top}_c(U)
 \ \Longrightarrow\ K_q(x)\preceq K_{(c)}\preceq\tau_{\rm seen}
 \ \Longrightarrow\ x\text{ is not rejected}.
\]
Stale reads only loosen the bound. Publications
made after earlier safe rejections remain valid: any $c$ retained
distinct candidates still supply $c$ witnesses, whether or not they are
the best $c$ of their group.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Reconstructed scoring and the query-only constant}

For $\gamma=2\langle\widehat p,\widehat r\rangle$, expand in real arithmetic:
\begin{align}
 \refineddist(q,x)
 &=\primarydist(q,x)+\|q'-\widehat r(x)\|_2^2+\gamma(x)
 \label{eq:5-refined-score}\\
 &=2\|q'\|_2^2+\|\widehat p+\widehat r\|_2^2-2\langle q',\widehat p+\widehat r\rangle\nonumber\\
 &=\|q'-\widehat p(x)-\widehat r(x)\|_2^2+\|q'\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:5-refined-constant}
\end{align}
The query constant preserves reconstructed-distance order \cite{jhq}.

Scalar scoring sums squared residual differences, then adds primary score/correction. Queries and fitting codebooks use shared memory.

\subsection{Mapping lanes to words and reducing partial sums}

For $\lrefine=L\in\{1,8,16,32\}$,
\[
 d_{\rm word}=32/B_R,\qquad
 \text{words of lane }a:\ a,a+L,a+2L,\ldots.
\]
A word holds four eight-bit or eight four-bit codes. Butterfly shuffles sum lane partials; lane zero writes the score.

For at least $k$ finite valid survivors with unique IDs, each round computes
\[
 i^*=\arg\min_{i<c}(D_{H,i},\mathrm{ID}_i),\quad d^*=D_{H,i^*},\quad
 D_{H,i^*}\leftarrow+\infty
\]
using all slots and emits $(\mathrm{ID}_{i^*},d^*)$: exact retained-pool top-$k$, without thread quotas. Underfull pools may repeat the smallest valid ID at infinity; all-invalid pools return invalid IDs. Tests meet the finite-entry premise.

Primary ties use positions, final ties IDs. Exclusions/quantisation remain; lane FP32 association may move near ties.
